target.title: fix(ui): prevent stale sidebar attention refreshes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users viewing sidebar health alerts could see cron or model-auth state revert when an older refresh on the same gateway connection completed after a newer refresh. The stale completion could also prune persisted dismissals against obsolete data and make an alert reappear unexpectedly.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each sidebar attention load now owns a generation token. Starting a replacement load, disconnecting, or detaching the component retires earlier generations, so only the current load may project cron/auth state, update the freshness timestamp, or prune dismissals.

## User Impact

Sidebar health alerts now remain based on the newest completed refresh during slow or overlapping gateway requests. This is a race-condition fix with no visual or configuration changes.

## Evidence

- Added a component-level deferred-request regression that starts two loads on the same client, completes the newer load first, then proves the older load cannot overwrite cron state, auth state, `loadedAtMs`, or persisted dismissals.
- Exact-head upstream CI is green on `32acfbf7d2e68795593a68fb7e38be037d9fa082`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29666771483
- Real Chromium before/after proof uses the actual Lit component and application context with one deterministic gateway client. The workflow pins current-main before SHA `b550c2cf9a8afff68958f98d71aa7e3c939f3e39` and PR after SHA `32acfbf7d2e68795593a68fb7e38be037d9fa082`: https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/actions/runs/29667390493
- Before: request B completes first, then stale request A restores cron `stale` and auth timestamp `1`, deletes the persisted dismissal, and visibly restores `1 cron job(s) failed`.
- After: request B remains authoritative after A completes: cron `current`, auth timestamp `2`, the B freshness timestamp is unchanged, the `cronFailed: current` dismissal remains, and the visible alert stays absent.
- Redacted proof artifact contains the before/after PNG screenshots and WebM recordings: https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/actions/runs/29667390493/artifacts/8436164573
- `git diff --check` passes on the exact PR head.
- Independent Codex adversarial review of the frozen diff found 0 actionable findings, including explicit disconnect, detach, and same-client reconnect lifecycle review.

AI-assisted: Codex was used for implementation, independent review, and deterministic browser proof; I reviewed and understand the change.
